note: Christian Religious Studies round 3 (part B): the Gospels - birth and early life of Jesus, baptism and temptation, discipleship, miracles, parables, Sermon on the Mount, mission of the disciples, great confession, transfiguration, triumphal entry and temple cleansing, Last Supper, trials and death, resurrection and ascension, Jesus' teachings about Himself - scripture-based and application items.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: When Mary asked the angel, 'How can this be, since I have no husband?' Gabriel replied that
questions.A: Joseph would become the father of the child after their wedding
questions.B: the Holy Spirit would come upon her and the child would be called the Son of God
questions.C: she should go to Bethlehem and wait for a sign from the priests
questions.D: her cousin Elizabeth would explain the mystery to her
questions.explanation: Luke 1:34-35: 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put Mary to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly, but changed his mind because
questions.A: the elders of Nazareth ordered him to complete the marriage
questions.B: Mary's parents paid him a large sum of money to keep the marriage
questions.C: an angel told him in a dream that the child was conceived of the Holy Spirit
questions.D: Elizabeth came from Judea to plead on Mary's behalf
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:19-21: the angel said, 'Do not fear to take Mary your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: Mary's song, 'He has put down the mighty from their thrones, and exalted those of low degree; he has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent empty away,' shows that the coming of Jesus would
questions.A: bring prosperity mainly to the priests in Jerusalem
questions.B: make Israel the richest nation on earth
questions.C: restore the throne of Herod to the family of David
questions.D: overturn human standards of power and wealth
questions.explanation: Luke 1:46-55 (the Magnificat): God's salvation lifts the humble and humbles the proud.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: Jesus was born in Bethlehem rather than Nazareth because
questions.A: Herod had ordered all descendants of David to live in Bethlehem
questions.B: Joseph went there to be enrolled in the census decreed by Caesar Augustus
questions.C: Mary's parents lived in Bethlehem and wanted her near them
questions.D: the wise men had told Joseph to go there
questions.explanation: Luke 2:1-5: Joseph went to Bethlehem, the city of David, to be enrolled with Mary, fulfilling Micah 5:2.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: The angel's message to the shepherds was 'good news of a great joy which will come to all the people'. The fact that it came first to shepherds shows that
questions.A: Bethlehem had no other inhabitants at the time
questions.B: the shepherds were priests who served in the temple
questions.C: the gospel is for the humble and lowly, not just the powerful
questions.D: the angels could not find the palace of Herod
questions.explanation: Luke 2:8-14: shepherds were poor and of low social standing, yet they were the first to hear of the Saviour's birth.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: Herod told the wise men, 'Go and search diligently for the child, and when you have found him bring me word, that I too may come and worship him.' His real intention was to
questions.A: send the child to be educated in Rome
questions.B: offer the child gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh
questions.C: adopt the child as his heir
questions.D: find the child and kill him
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:8, 13, 16: warned in a dream, the wise men did not return, and Herod killed all the boys in Bethlehem aged two and under.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: A politician publicly praises a rival while secretly plotting to destroy him. His conduct resembles that of
questions.A: Simeon towards the child in the temple
questions.B: Herod towards the infant Jesus
questions.C: the shepherds towards Mary and Joseph
questions.D: Zechariah towards his son John
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:7-8: Herod's pretended desire to worship masked a plan to murder the child.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: When Jesus' parents found him in the temple after three days, he said, 'Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?' This shows that at twelve Jesus
questions.A: was rebuking his parents for going to the Passover
questions.B: had decided to leave his parents and live with the priests
questions.C: was already aware of his unique relationship with God
questions.D: had been adopted by the teachers of the law
questions.explanation: Luke 2:49: Jesus' words reveal his consciousness of God as his Father; yet he went home and was obedient to his parents.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: After the incident in the temple, Jesus 'went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them; and Jesus increased in wisdom and in stature, and in favour with God and man'. A teenager who feels that being religious frees him from obeying his parents should learn from this that
questions.A: parents should not question children about religious matters
questions.B: Jesus obeyed only because he was too young to leave home
questions.C: wisdom is gained by staying in the temple rather than at home
questions.D: obedience to parents is part of growing in favour with God
questions.explanation: Luke 2:51-52: Jesus, though conscious of his divine sonship, submitted to his earthly parents.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus
questions.q: The prophetess Anna, who was at the temple when Jesus was presented, responded by
questions.A: warning Mary that Herod was seeking to kill the child
questions.B: giving thanks to God and speaking of the child to all who were looking for redemption
questions.C: asking Joseph to leave the child in the temple to be trained
questions.D: offering the pair of turtledoves required by the law
questions.explanation: Luke 2:36-38: Anna, a widow of eighty-four, gave thanks and spoke of him to all who waited for the redemption of Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: John tried to prevent Jesus from being baptised, saying, 'I need to be baptised by you.' Jesus insisted because
questions.A: he wanted to become one of John's disciples
questions.B: he had sins that needed to be washed away
questions.C: it was fitting for him to fulfil all righteousness
questions.D: the crowd expected every teacher to be baptised
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:14-15: Jesus, though sinless, identified himself with the people he came to save.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: Immediately after his baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted. This sequence shows that
questions.A: the devil has authority over those who are baptised
questions.B: the Spirit was punishing Jesus for being baptised
questions.C: Jesus had lost the approval God gave him at the Jordan
questions.D: spiritual high points may be followed by severe testing
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:1: the same Spirit who descended at the baptism led Jesus into the wilderness; testing followed the declaration of sonship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: In the temptation to turn stones into bread, the devil was urging Jesus to
questions.A: feed the crowds of Galilee so that they would make him king
questions.B: use his divine power to satisfy his own needs apart from God's will
questions.C: prove that he could survive without any food at all
questions.D: reject the Passover bread and eat ordinary bread instead
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3-4: Jesus answered, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: On the pinnacle of the temple the devil quoted Psalm 91, 'He will give his angels charge of you.' Jesus replied, 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God,' teaching that
questions.A: angels no longer protect the people of God as they did in the days of David
questions.B: the Psalms should not be quoted by anyone except the priests in the temple
questions.C: scripture must not be twisted to justify testing God with reckless acts
questions.D: the pinnacle of the temple was not a holy place from which to pray
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:5-7: Jesus refused to demand a spectacular sign from God, using scripture rightly against scripture misused.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: A church member says, 'God will protect me, so I will drive at top speed without a seat belt.' His attitude is like the temptation Jesus rejected when he said,
questions.A: 'Get behind me, Satan!'
questions.B: 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'
questions.C: 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve.'
questions.D: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God.'
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:7: deliberately courting danger and expecting God to intervene is putting God to the test.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: The devil offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if he would fall down and worship him. This temptation was to
questions.A: become the governor of Judea under the Roman emperor
questions.B: gain his rightful kingship by a short cut that avoided the cross
questions.C: abandon Galilee and preach only in foreign lands
questions.D: share his authority equally with the devil
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:8-10: the devil offered glory without suffering; Jesus chose the way of obedience to the Father.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: In each of the three temptations Jesus answered the devil with
questions.A: a command to the angels to drive the devil away
questions.B: a miracle that proved he was the Son of God
questions.C: a quotation from the book of Deuteronomy
questions.D: a promise to obey the devil after his ministry ended
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:4, 7, 10 quote Deuteronomy 8:3, 6:16 and 6:13; Jesus overcame with the written word of God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: A candidate is offered examination answers by a friend and refuses, saying, 'I would rather fail honestly.' His refusal reflects the principle Jesus applied when he rejected
questions.A: the crowd's attempt to make him king by force
questions.B: John's attempt to prevent him from being baptised
questions.C: Peter's request to build three booths on the mountain
questions.D: the offer of the kingdoms of the world in exchange for worshipping the devil
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:8-10: like Jesus, the student refuses to gain a good end by a wrong means.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: Luke notes that after the temptations the devil 'departed from him until an opportune time'. This suggests that
questions.A: the devil was completely destroyed in the wilderness
questions.B: temptation is not defeated once for all but returns at other moments in life
questions.C: Jesus would never face any further testing
questions.D: the devil had become one of Jesus' followers
questions.explanation: Luke 4:13: the devil returned in other forms, for instance through Peter (Matthew 16:23) and at Gethsemane.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus told Simon to put out into the deep and let down the nets, Simon said, 'Master, we toiled all night and took nothing! But at your word I will let down the nets.' This shows that discipleship requires
questions.A: working at night rather than during the day
questions.B: fishing skill that can be used for the service of God
questions.C: obedience to the word of Jesus even against one's own experience
questions.D: waiting until the evidence is clear before acting
questions.explanation: Luke 5:4-6: Simon obeyed despite a fruitless night, and the nets nearly broke with fish.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Seeing the great catch of fish, Simon Peter fell at Jesus' knees and said, 'Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.' Jesus responded,
questions.A: 'Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests.'
questions.B: 'Get behind me, Satan! You are a hindrance to me.'
questions.C: 'O man of little faith, why did you doubt?'
questions.D: 'Do not be afraid; henceforth you will be catching men.'
questions.explanation: Luke 5:8-11: rather than leave him, Jesus called Peter to a new task, and the fishermen left everything and followed him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: To the man who said, 'Lord, let me first go and bury my father,' Jesus replied, 'Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but as for you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.' Jesus was teaching that
questions.A: Christians should not attend the funerals of their relatives
questions.B: the call of the kingdom takes priority over every other claim, however legitimate
questions.C: the man's father was still alive and did not need burial
questions.D: only priests were permitted to bury the dead in Israel
questions.explanation: Luke 9:59-60: the demands of discipleship are urgent and must not be postponed indefinitely for family duties.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.' A convert who keeps longing for his former life of crime is
questions.A: like Peter, who left his nets to follow Jesus
questions.B: a good example of the total commitment Jesus demanded
questions.C: like the ploughman who looks back and cannot plough a straight furrow
questions.D: like Zacchaeus, who restored fourfold what he had taken
questions.explanation: Luke 9:62: single-minded commitment is required; divided loyalty makes a disciple unfit for kingdom service.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told the rich young ruler, 'Sell what you possess and give to the poor... and come, follow me,' because
questions.A: the young man had gained his riches by fraud
questions.B: the disciples needed money to fund their mission
questions.C: poverty is required of every person who follows Jesus
questions.D: his wealth stood between him and wholehearted devotion to God
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:21-22: the man went away sorrowful because he had great possessions; his riches were his real master.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Pharisees asked why Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners, he replied,
questions.A: 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.'
questions.B: 'Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.'
questions.C: 'The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.'
questions.D: 'Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone.'
questions.explanation: Mark 2:15-17: Jesus called Levi the tax collector and defended eating with sinners, whom he came to call.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus warned would-be disciples to count the cost, like a man who intends to build a tower or a king going to war. The point is that
questions.A: Christians should prepare for physical warfare against unbelievers
questions.B: only wealthy people who can afford towers should become disciples
questions.C: one should consider seriously what following Jesus demands before committing
questions.D: discipleship can be abandoned whenever it becomes costly
questions.explanation: Luke 14:28-33: 'whoever of you does not renounce all that he has cannot be my disciple'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student who publicly identifies as a Christian in a hostile hostel and accepts mockery for it is fulfilling Jesus' word that a disciple must
questions.A: avoid contact with unbelievers altogether
questions.B: hide his faith until conditions become favourable
questions.C: leave school and join a monastery
questions.D: deny himself, take up his cross daily and follow him
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23: bearing the cross means accepting shame and suffering for the sake of Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'If any one comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother... yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.' By 'hate' he meant that
questions.A: disciples must break off all relations with their families as soon as they begin to follow him
questions.B: love for him must so far exceed every other love that others seem like hatred by comparison
questions.C: family members are the chief enemies of the kingdom of God and must be treated with suspicion
questions.D: disciples should neglect the care of their aged parents in order to devote all their time to him
questions.explanation: Luke 14:26: a Semitic idiom for 'love less'; Jesus elsewhere commanded honour for parents (Mark 7:9-13).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Before healing the paralytic lowered through the roof, Jesus said, 'My son, your sins are forgiven,' and the scribes objected. Jesus then healed the man in order to
questions.A: reward the four friends for their hard work
questions.B: prove that the man's paralysis was caused by his own sin
questions.C: show that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins
questions.D: punish the scribes for their unbelief
questions.explanation: Mark 2:5-12: the visible healing confirmed the invisible authority to forgive sins.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The woman with the flow of blood touched Jesus' garment secretly, but Jesus insisted on finding out who had touched him because
questions.A: the disciples had asked him to identify the thief
questions.B: he intended to rebuke her for making him ceremonially unclean
questions.C: he wanted to know who had stolen from him in the crowd
questions.D: he wanted her to receive not only healing but also open assurance of faith and peace
questions.explanation: Mark 5:25-34: 'Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace, and be healed of your disease.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jairus was told, 'Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?' Jesus said to him,
questions.A: 'Your faith has made you well; go in peace.'
questions.B: 'Do not fear, only believe.'
questions.C: 'Why are you afraid? Have you no faith?'
questions.D: 'Talitha cumi', which means 'Little girl, arise'.
questions.explanation: Mark 5:35-36: Jesus encouraged the ruler to keep faith in the face of death and then raised the girl.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the disciples wanted to send the crowd away to buy food, Jesus said, 'You give them something to eat,' and then fed five thousand with five loaves and two fish. This teaches that
questions.A: large crowds should be dispersed before evening
questions.B: disciples should never carry food when travelling
questions.C: Jesus can multiply the little we offer to meet the needs of many
questions.D: bread and fish are the only foods Christians should eat
questions.explanation: Mark 6:35-44: the disciples' small resources, placed in Jesus' hands, fed the multitude with twelve baskets left over.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the pool of Bethzatha Jesus asked a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years, 'Do you want to be healed?' The man complained that he had no one to put him into the pool. Jesus
questions.A: asked his disciples to lift him into the pool
questions.B: carried him into the pool when the water was troubled
questions.C: told him to wait for an angel to come and heal him
questions.D: healed him with a word on the Sabbath without using the pool at all
questions.explanation: John 5:5-9: 'Rise, take up your pallet, and walk'; the healing led to conflict because it was the Sabbath.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The blind man healed in John 9 said to the Pharisees, 'One thing I know, that though I was blind, now I see.' His answer illustrates that
questions.A: blind people should not be questioned by religious leaders
questions.B: personal experience of Christ's power is a testimony that arguments cannot overturn
questions.C: the man did not know who had healed him
questions.D: the Pharisees had healed him themselves
questions.explanation: John 9:24-25: the man could not settle theological debates but he could not deny what Jesus had done for him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A Christian who is asked to break the law by his employer replies, 'God who healed my child can also find me another job.' His confidence resembles that of the centurion who told Jesus,
questions.A: 'Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.'
questions.B: 'Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.'
questions.C: 'Only say the word, and my servant will be healed.'
questions.D: 'Lord, I believe; help my unbelief!'
questions.explanation: Matthew 8:8-10: the centurion trusted the authority of Jesus' word alone, and Jesus marvelled at such faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The Gerasene demoniac, once healed, begged to go with Jesus, but Jesus told him,
questions.A: 'Come and see where I am staying, and remain with me until the feast.'
questions.B: 'Follow me, and I will make you a fisher of men, for the harvest is plentiful.'
questions.C: 'See that you say nothing to any one, but go and show yourself to the priest.'
questions.D: 'Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you.'
questions.explanation: Mark 5:18-20: the healed man became a witness in the Decapolis, in contrast to others whom Jesus told to keep silent.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the ruler of the synagogue was indignant that Jesus healed a crippled woman on the Sabbath, Jesus called him a hypocrite because
questions.A: he had healed several people himself on the Sabbath in previous years without any complaint from the elders
questions.B: he would untie his ox or ass on the Sabbath to water it but objected to a daughter of Abraham being loosed
questions.C: the woman was his own relative and he had refused for eighteen years to help her in any way at all
questions.D: he had invited Jesus to the synagogue specifically to heal her and then denied doing so before the people
questions.explanation: Luke 13:10-17: Jesus exposed the inconsistency of caring for animals on the Sabbath while denying relief to a suffering person.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The raising of the widow's son at Nain was prompted by
questions.A: the faith of the widow, who touched his garment
questions.B: the request of the elders of the town
questions.C: Jesus' compassion when he saw the weeping mother
questions.D: the disciples' desire to see a sign
questions.explanation: Luke 7:11-15: 'When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, Do not weep.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the sower, the seed sown on rocky ground represents those who
questions.A: hear the word, understand it and bear fruit a hundredfold
questions.B: hear the word but the cares of the world and the delight in riches choke it
questions.C: hear the word and immediately the evil one snatches it away
questions.D: receive the word with joy but fall away when tribulation comes because they have no root
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:20-21: shallow enthusiasm without depth cannot survive persecution.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church member who receives the word gladly but abandons the faith the moment his family opposes him is like the seed sown
questions.A: along the path, where the birds came and devoured it
questions.B: on rocky ground, where it sprang up quickly but withered in the sun
questions.C: among thorns, which grew up and choked it
questions.D: on good soil, where it brought forth grain
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:5-6, 20-21: no root means no endurance under pressure.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the weeds, the householder told his servants not to gather the weeds before the harvest because
questions.A: the enemy who sowed them would return and remove them
questions.B: the weeds would eventually turn into wheat if left alone
questions.C: in gathering the weeds they might root up the wheat along with them
questions.D: the servants were too tired to work in the field
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:24-30: final separation of the righteous and the wicked belongs to God at the close of the age.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A pastor decides to expel every member he suspects of secret sin. The parable of the weeds cautions him that
questions.A: the enemy has no power to sow weeds among the wheat once the pastor has purified the church
questions.B: the church should contain only perfect people, so every suspected sinner must be removed at once
questions.C: weeds should be pulled up as soon as they are noticed, before they can spread to the whole field
questions.D: judgment and separation belong to God at the harvest, and hasty uprooting harms the wheat
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:29-30, 36-43: the Son of man will send his angels to gather out of his kingdom all causes of sin at the end.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the labourers in the vineyard, those hired at the eleventh hour received the same wage as those hired first. The parable teaches that
questions.A: employers should pay all workers exactly the same regardless of hours
questions.B: God's generosity in the kingdom is not measured by human ideas of merit
questions.C: latecomers to the faith will have a higher place in heaven
questions.D: the first labourers were cheated by a dishonest householder
questions.explanation: Matthew 20:1-16: 'Do you begrudge my generosity?... So the last will be first, and the first last.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the wise and foolish maidens, the foolish ones were shut out because
questions.A: they refused to share their oil with the others when the bridegroom's arrival was delayed
questions.B: they fell asleep while the wise maidens stayed awake and kept watch through the night
questions.C: they took no oil with their lamps and were absent buying some when the bridegroom came
questions.D: they arrived at the feast before the bridegroom and were sent away for their impatience
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:1-13: all ten slept, but only the wise were prepared; 'Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the sheep and the goats, the King says, 'As you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you did it to me.' The parable teaches that
questions.A: the final judgment is based on the number of prayers said
questions.B: sheep are more valuable than goats in the eyes of God
questions.C: only those who preach the gospel will enter the kingdom
questions.D: practical care for the needy is treated as service rendered to Christ himself
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:31-46: feeding the hungry, welcoming strangers, clothing the naked and visiting the sick and imprisoned are the marks of the righteous.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student says she loves Jesus but ignores a hungry classmate sitting beside her every day. The parable of the sheep and the goats warns that
questions.A: her love for Jesus is enough since she did nothing wrong
questions.B: neglect of the needy is counted as neglect of Christ himself
questions.C: feeding classmates is the duty of the school and not of students
questions.D: only the rich are expected to help those in need
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:45: 'As you did it not to one of the least of these, you did it not to me.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, Abraham refused to send Lazarus to warn the rich man's brothers because
questions.A: the brothers had already died and joined the rich man
questions.B: Lazarus was too weak from his sores to make the journey
questions.C: they had Moses and the prophets, and would not be convinced even if someone rose from the dead
questions.D: the great chasm made it impossible for anyone to leave paradise
questions.explanation: Luke 16:27-31: those who ignore the scriptures will not be persuaded by miracles.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The parable of the two sons, one who said 'I will not' but later went to the vineyard and one who said 'I go, sir' but did not, was told to show that
questions.A: vineyard work was reserved for the eldest son, while the younger son was expected to remain at home with his mother
questions.B: sons should always obey their fathers immediately without argument, since delayed obedience is the same as disobedience
questions.C: the first son was punished for his rude answer even though he later did the work his father had asked him to do
questions.D: tax collectors and harlots who repented were entering the kingdom before the religious leaders who only professed obedience
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:28-32: actual obedience matters more than verbal profession.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church officer promises to organise the youth camp, does nothing, and later criticises a reluctant member who eventually did the work. According to the parable of the two sons, the one who did the father's will was
questions.A: the officer who made the promise in front of everyone
questions.B: the reluctant member who at first refused but later did the work
questions.C: neither of them, since both showed a wrong attitude
questions.D: both equally, since intentions count as much as actions
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:31: 'Which of the two did the will of his father?' They said, 'The first.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the wicked tenants, the owner finally sent his son, saying, 'They will respect my son.' The tenants killed him. The parable pointed to
questions.A: the destruction of the vineyards of Galilee by the Samaritans during the reign of Herod the Great
questions.B: the failure of the Roman governors to protect Jewish farmers from bandits in the hills of Galilee
questions.C: the rejection and killing of Jesus by the leaders of Israel after they had rejected the prophets
questions.D: the need for landlords to collect their rent in person rather than sending servants to do it
questions.explanation: Mark 12:1-12: the chief priests perceived that he had told the parable against them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'You are the salt of the earth; but if salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltness be restored?' A Christian who behaves exactly like his corrupt colleagues is
questions.A: salt that preserves society from decay
questions.B: a lamp placed on a stand to give light to the house
questions.C: a city set on a hill that cannot be hid
questions.D: salt that has lost its taste and is good for nothing
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:13: disciples who lose their distinctive character lose their usefulness to the world.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'Think not that I have come to abolish the law and the prophets; I have come not to abolish them but to fulfil them.' He then taught that anger and lust break the commandments against murder and adultery. This shows that Jesus
questions.A: abolished the Ten Commandments for his followers
questions.B: required a righteousness that goes deeper than outward acts to the heart
questions.C: regarded murder and adultery as minor offences
questions.D: wanted the scribes to add more rules to the law
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:17-28: 'Unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'If you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother.' A choir member who refuses to speak to another member but still sings every Sunday should
questions.A: leave the choir permanently until the other member apologises
questions.B: continue singing, since worship is more important than relationships
questions.C: seek reconciliation first, because broken relationships hinder acceptable worship
questions.D: report the matter to the pastor and wait for judgment
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:23-24: God values reconciliation with one's brother above religious offerings.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus taught, 'Let what you say be simply Yes or No; anything more than this comes from evil.' This teaches that Christians should
questions.A: answer every question with a single word
questions.B: never appear in court to give evidence
questions.C: swear only by heaven and not by earth
questions.D: be so truthful that oaths are unnecessary
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:33-37: a disciple's plain word should be as reliable as a sworn oath.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'If any one strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.' Jesus was teaching his followers to
questions.A: provoke their enemies until they strike again
questions.B: renounce personal revenge and overcome evil with generosity
questions.C: avoid ever defending the weak against injustice
questions.D: report every assault to the Roman authorities
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:38-42: the principle 'an eye for an eye' was replaced by non-retaliation and readiness to give.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus commanded, 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good.' The reason given for loving enemies is that
questions.A: the Roman law required Jews to love their oppressors
questions.B: enemies will always become friends if they are loved
questions.C: it reflects the impartial goodness of God the Father
questions.D: loving enemies earns a place among the Pharisees
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:44-48: children resemble their Father, who shows kindness to the just and the unjust alike.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A businessman announces his donation to the church over the loudspeaker so that everyone will applaud. Jesus warned that such givers
questions.A: are the salt of the earth
questions.B: will receive a double reward from the Father
questions.C: should give even more to gain approval
questions.D: have already received their reward
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:1-4: 'When you give alms, sound no trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do... they have received their reward.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the Lord's Prayer the petition 'forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors' is followed by the warning that
questions.A: debts must be repaid in full before any prayer can be heard by the Father who is in heaven
questions.B: if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses
questions.C: only debts owed to fellow Christians need to be forgiven, while others may be collected in full
questions.D: God forgives without any condition whatever a person does, so forgiving others is optional
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:12, 14-15: receiving God's forgiveness is bound up with extending forgiveness to others.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal... For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.' Jesus was teaching that
questions.A: money should be hidden where thieves cannot find it
questions.B: Christians should not own houses, land or savings of any kind
questions.C: what a person values most determines the direction of his heart and life
questions.D: earthly wealth is a sure sign of God's blessing
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:19-21, 24: 'You cannot serve God and mammon.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them.' Jesus said this to teach his disciples
questions.A: that birds are more valuable than human beings
questions.B: that work is unnecessary because God feeds those who trust him
questions.C: that farming is a less spiritual occupation than fishing
questions.D: not to be anxious about food and clothing but to seek first the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:25-34: 'Seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be yours as well.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'Not every one who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father.' He compared those who hear his words and do them to
questions.A: a foolish man who built his house upon the sand
questions.B: a wise man who built his house upon the rock
questions.C: a lamp hidden under a bushel
questions.D: a tree that bears evil fruit
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:21-27: the house on the rock withstood rain, floods and wind because it was founded on obedience.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'Enter by the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way is easy that leads to destruction.' Jesus meant that
questions.A: large churches are always on the way to destruction
questions.B: Christians should build narrow gates at their homes
questions.C: the way of true discipleship is demanding and followed by few
questions.D: salvation is impossible for most people
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:13-14: 'The gate is narrow and the way is hard that leads to life, and those who find it are few.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus sent out the twelve with the instruction, 'Preach as you go, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You received without pay, give without pay.' The last sentence forbids
questions.A: preaching to people who had not first paid the disciples
questions.B: accepting food and lodging from those who received the message
questions.C: healing people who could not pay the temple tax
questions.D: turning the ministry of healing and preaching into a means of making money
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:7-8: the gifts of the kingdom were freely received and must be freely given.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A preacher charges a fixed fee before he will pray for the sick. He violates the principle Jesus gave when he said,
questions.A: 'The labourer deserves his food.'
questions.B: 'You received without pay, give without pay.'
questions.C: 'Shake off the dust from your feet.'
questions.D: 'Be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.'
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:8: healing is a gift of God's grace and must not be sold.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told the disciples to take no gold, silver or copper, no bag, no two tunics, no sandals or staff, 'for the labourer deserves his food'. This meant that they should
questions.A: expect to starve as a sign of their devotion
questions.B: beg for money from door to door in every town
questions.C: depend on God's provision through the hospitality of those they served
questions.D: carry only what they could steal from unbelievers
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:9-11: travelling light expressed trust in God and urgency in the mission.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus instructed the disciples that if any town would not receive them or listen to their words, they should
questions.A: report the town to the Roman governor
questions.B: call down fire from heaven to destroy it
questions.C: remain there until the people repented
questions.D: shake off the dust from their feet as they left that town
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:14: the gesture was a solemn testimony that the town had rejected the message and was responsible for its choice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus warned, 'Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.' He meant that the disciples should be
questions.A: aggressive towards their opponents like a serpent striking
questions.B: prudent in dealing with danger while remaining pure in motive and conduct
questions.C: silent and passive like sheep being led to slaughter
questions.D: cunning enough to deceive those who threatened them
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:16: wisdom without harm; prudence without dishonesty.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the seventy returned with joy, saying, 'Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!' Jesus told them to
questions.A: return to the villages and cast out more demons
questions.B: keep the power secret until after the resurrection
questions.C: rejoice rather that their names were written in heaven
questions.D: demand payment from those they had delivered
questions.explanation: Luke 10:17-20: the greatest cause for joy is salvation itself, not spectacular power.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told the disciples, 'When they deliver you up, do not be anxious how you are to speak or what you are to say... for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.' This promise concerned
questions.A: preaching the Sermon on the Mount
questions.B: the writing of the gospels many years later
questions.C: speaking in foreign tongues at Pentecost
questions.D: help in bearing witness when brought before councils and rulers
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:17-20: persecution would give opportunity for testimony, and the Spirit would supply the words.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A missionary moves on from a village that repeatedly drives him out, instead of forcing himself on the people, and later returns when invited. He is following Jesus' instruction to
questions.A: stay in one house and not move from house to house
questions.B: shake off the dust from his feet and leave a town that will not receive him
questions.C: take neither bag nor money for the journey
questions.D: greet no one on the road
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:14 and Luke 10:10-11: the disciples were not to compel acceptance but to move on with a solemn witness.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus asked, 'Who do men say that the Son of man is?' the disciples reported that people said he was
questions.A: a carpenter's son from Nazareth and nothing more
questions.B: the Messiah, the Son of the living God
questions.C: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah or one of the prophets
questions.D: Beelzebul, the prince of demons
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:13-14: popular opinion honoured Jesus as a prophet but fell short of recognising him as the Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told Peter, 'Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona! For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.' This shows that
questions.A: the confession was a lucky guess that Jesus rewarded
questions.B: Peter had studied the scriptures more than the other disciples
questions.C: Peter's father Jonah had told him who Jesus was
questions.D: true recognition of Jesus as the Christ comes by divine revelation
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:17: Peter's insight was a gift from the Father, not a human deduction.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Peter's confession Jesus charged the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ, because
questions.A: he was not yet certain that he was the Messiah
questions.B: the people expected a political Messiah and would misunderstand his mission
questions.C: the disciples might be arrested immediately by Herod
questions.D: only the high priest was permitted to announce the Messiah
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:20-21: from that time he began to teach that he must suffer, die and rise, correcting their expectations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus foretold his suffering and death, Peter rebuked him, saying, 'God forbid, Lord! This shall never happen to you.' Jesus replied, 'Get behind me, Satan!' because Peter was
questions.A: possessed by an evil spirit at that moment
questions.B: secretly plotting with the chief priests against Jesus
questions.C: on the side of men, not of God, in opposing the way of the cross
questions.D: trying to take the leadership of the disciples from Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:22-23: Peter's love expressed the same temptation the devil offered - glory without suffering.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church member advises his pastor to stop preaching against a powerful politician 'so that trouble does not come to you'. His well-meant advice resembles
questions.A: Thomas' demand to see the nail prints
questions.B: Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ
questions.C: James and John's request to sit at Jesus' right and left
questions.D: Peter's rebuke of Jesus after the great confession
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:22-23: avoiding suffering at the cost of God's will is a temptation even when it comes from a friend.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Immediately after the great confession, Jesus said, 'If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me. For whoever would save his life will lose it.' This linked Peter's confession to
questions.A: the promise that the disciples would never suffer
questions.B: the cost of following a Messiah whose path led to the cross
questions.C: the building of a church on the rock of Caesarea Philippi
questions.D: the immediate establishment of an earthly kingdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:24-26: confessing Christ means sharing his way of self-denial and suffering.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The great confession took place in the district of
questions.A: Bethany near Jerusalem
questions.B: Capernaum by the sea
questions.C: Caesarea Philippi
questions.D: Nazareth in Galilee
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:13: 'When Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples...'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said to Peter, 'I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.' In Acts, Peter used this authority when he
questions.A: appointed himself high priest in place of Caiaphas
questions.B: refused to allow the Gentiles to be baptised without circumcision
questions.C: closed the temple in Jerusalem to all non-Jewish worshippers
questions.D: opened the door of faith to the Jews at Pentecost and to the Gentiles at the house of Cornelius
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:19; Acts 2 and 10: Peter's preaching admitted first Jews and then Gentiles into the church.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The three disciples Jesus took up the mountain of transfiguration were
questions.A: Peter, Andrew and Philip
questions.B: Peter, James and John
questions.C: James, John and Thomas
questions.D: Matthew, Mark and Luke
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1: 'Jesus took with him Peter and James and John his brother, and led them up a high mountain apart.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The appearance of Moses and Elijah with Jesus at the transfiguration signified that
questions.A: Jesus was only one prophet among equals
questions.B: Moses and Elijah had returned to lead the nation of Israel
questions.C: the law and the prophets bore witness to Jesus and found their fulfilment in him
questions.D: the disciples should build a permanent shrine on the mountain
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3: Moses represents the law and Elijah the prophets; both pointed forward to Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter said, 'Lord, it is well that we are here; if you wish, I will make three booths.' His suggestion showed that he
questions.A: was trying to send Moses and Elijah away
questions.B: had understood that Jesus was greater than Moses and Elijah
questions.C: expected Jesus to establish his kingdom on the mountain that day
questions.D: wanted to prolong the glorious moment and did not yet grasp that the path led to the cross
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:4-5; Luke 9:33 notes that Peter did not know what he said; the voice from the cloud corrected the emphasis.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The voice from the cloud at the transfiguration said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.' The command 'listen to him' emphasised that
questions.A: Moses and Elijah were to be ignored from then on because their words had lost all value
questions.B: Jesus' teaching, including his prediction of suffering, carried God's own authority
questions.C: the disciples were to write down everything Jesus said from that day until the ascension
questions.D: only Peter, James and John were permitted to hear Jesus teach for the rest of his ministry
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:5: the disciples had resisted the teaching about the cross; God commanded them to heed it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded the three disciples to tell no one the vision until
questions.A: Elijah had come and restored all things
questions.B: they had told the other nine apostles
questions.C: the Son of man had been raised from the dead
questions.D: the Passover had been celebrated in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:9: only after the resurrection would the glory of the transfiguration be rightly understood.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the disciples asked, 'Why do the scribes say that first Elijah must come?' Jesus answered that Elijah had already come and they did not know him. He was referring to
questions.A: Simeon in the temple
questions.B: Moses on the mountain
questions.C: the prophet Malachi
questions.D: John the Baptist
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:10-13: 'Then the disciples understood that he was speaking to them of John the Baptist.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A believer wishes she could stay in the joy of a retreat for ever and dreads returning to the difficulties at home. Her feeling resembles that of
questions.A: Judas, who complained about the wasted ointment
questions.B: Peter, who wanted to build three booths on the mountain
questions.C: Martha, who was distracted with much serving
questions.D: the rich young ruler, who went away sorrowful
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:4: like Peter, she would prolong the mountain-top experience, but discipleship continues in the valley below.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the foot of the mountain the disciples could not heal a boy with an epileptic spirit. Jesus attributed their failure to
questions.A: the absence of Peter, James and John
questions.B: the boy's father's unbelief
questions.C: their little faith
questions.D: the fact that it was the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:19-20: 'Because of your little faith... if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, nothing will be impossible to you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: The crowd at the triumphal entry shouted, 'Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!' The title 'Son of David' showed that they
questions.A: thought Jesus was a Levite from the tribe of the priests
questions.B: believed Jesus was the physical son of King Herod
questions.C: were mocking Jesus for claiming royal descent
questions.D: recognised Jesus as the promised Messiah of David's line
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:9: 'Hosanna' means 'save now', and 'Son of David' was a messianic title.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: By riding into Jerusalem on a donkey rather than a horse, Jesus presented himself as
questions.A: a poor man who could not afford a horse
questions.B: a humble king of peace, not a military conqueror
questions.C: a pilgrim like every other Galilean at the feast
questions.D: a prophet in the tradition of Elijah
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:4-5 (Zechariah 9:9): 'your king is coming to you, humble, and mounted on an ass'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: When the Pharisees asked Jesus to rebuke his disciples for their praise, he replied,
questions.A: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer.'
questions.B: 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.'
questions.C: 'If these were silent, the very stones would cry out.'
questions.D: 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.'
questions.explanation: Luke 19:39-40: the praise was fitting and could not be suppressed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: As Jesus drew near and saw Jerusalem he wept over it because
questions.A: his disciples had abandoned him at the gate and fled back to Galilee
questions.B: the crowd that welcomed him was too small for a royal entry into the city
questions.C: the temple had been cleansed by the Romans before he could reach it
questions.D: the city did not know the time of its visitation and would be destroyed
questions.explanation: Luke 19:41-44: Jesus foresaw the destruction of the city that rejected the things that make for peace.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: Jesus drove the traders out of the temple and overturned the tables of the money-changers, saying they had made God's house 'a den of robbers'. The traders were guilty of
questions.A: selling animals that the law did not permit as sacrifices
questions.B: exploiting worshippers and turning the court of the Gentiles into a market
questions.C: refusing to pay the temple tax to the priests
questions.D: trading on the Sabbath against the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Mark 11:15-17: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations'; commerce had displaced the worship of the Gentiles.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: A church turns its Sunday service into a marketplace where members are pressured to buy the pastor's products at inflated prices. This resembles the situation Jesus condemned when he
questions.A: rebuked the Pharisees for their long prayers
questions.B: cursed the fig tree that had leaves but no fruit
questions.C: cleansed the temple of those who bought and sold
questions.D: wept over the city of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Mark 11:15-17: turning worship into an occasion for profit makes God's house a den of robbers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: After the cleansing of the temple, the chief priests and scribes sought a way to destroy Jesus, but they feared him because
questions.A: the money-changers had joined his disciples
questions.B: the Roman soldiers were guarding him
questions.C: he had threatened to burn down the temple
questions.D: all the multitude was astonished at his teaching
questions.explanation: Mark 11:18: the leaders' hostility was held in check by Jesus' popularity with the people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: The blind and the lame came to Jesus in the temple after its cleansing and he healed them. This showed that
questions.A: healing was only permitted in the temple courts
questions.B: the temple, cleansed of trade, became again a place of God's mercy
questions.C: the chief priests approved of Jesus' actions
questions.D: the money-changers had been healing people before
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:14-16: the house of prayer became a house of healing, while children cried 'Hosanna to the Son of David'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: When the chief priests asked Jesus, 'By what authority are you doing these things?' he answered with a question about
questions.A: which commandment was the greatest
questions.B: whose image and inscription was on the coin
questions.C: whether the baptism of John was from heaven or from men
questions.D: whose wife the woman with seven husbands would be
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:23-27: the leaders could not answer without condemning themselves, so Jesus declined to tell them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the Last Supper Jesus took bread, blessed and broke it, and said, 'Take, eat; this is my body.' The bread symbolised
questions.A: the loaves that fed the five thousand
questions.B: the manna eaten by Israel in the wilderness
questions.C: the unleavened bread of the Passover only
questions.D: his body given in death for his followers
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:26; Luke 22:19: 'This is my body which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said of the cup, 'This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.' The cup therefore signified
questions.A: the wine of the Passover meal and nothing more
questions.B: a new covenant established by his sacrificial death
questions.C: the blood of the lambs slain in the temple
questions.D: the judgment coming upon Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:28: Jesus' death inaugurated the new covenant foretold in Jeremiah 31.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the disciples disputed about which of them was the greatest, Jesus said, 'Let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the leader as one who serves.' He supported this by pointing out that
questions.A: Peter had been chosen as the greatest apostle
questions.B: the kings of the Gentiles were called benefactors
questions.C: he himself was among them as one who serves
questions.D: the youngest disciple would sit at his right hand
questions.explanation: Luke 22:24-27: 'I am among you as one who serves.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus told Peter, 'Simon, Simon, behold, Satan demanded to have you, that he might sift you like wheat, but I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail; and when you have turned again, strengthen your brethren.' This shows that
questions.A: Peter was being removed from the company of the apostles
questions.B: Peter would never deny Jesus because Jesus had prayed for him
questions.C: Satan had taken complete control of Peter
questions.D: Jesus foresaw Peter's fall but also his restoration and future ministry
questions.explanation: Luke 22:31-32: Jesus' intercession ensured that Peter's failure would not be final.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus began to wash the disciples' feet, Peter protested, 'You shall never wash my feet.' Jesus answered,
questions.A: 'Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona!'
questions.B: 'If I do not wash you, you have no part in me.'
questions.C: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'
questions.D: 'Feed my sheep.'
questions.explanation: John 13:8: Peter then asked to be washed entirely, and Jesus explained the meaning of the act.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A company director who insists on serving food to the cleaners at the staff party, rather than being served, is practising what Jesus taught when he
questions.A: washed the disciples' feet and told them to wash one another's feet
questions.B: told the disciples to take no bag or money for the journey
questions.C: overturned the tables of the money-changers
questions.D: cursed the fig tree that bore no fruit
questions.explanation: John 13:12-15: 'I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said at the supper, 'A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; even as I have loved you.' The newness of this commandment lay in
questions.A: its standard: the self-giving love of Jesus himself
questions.B: the fact that love had never been commanded before
questions.C: its limitation to the twelve apostles only
questions.D: its replacement of the command to love God
questions.explanation: John 13:34-35: 'By this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After Judas received the morsel and went out, John notes, 'and it was night'. This detail suggests
questions.A: the spiritual darkness of Judas' betrayal
questions.B: that the supper was held later than usual
questions.C: that the disciples had run out of lamp oil
questions.D: that the Passover always began at midnight
questions.explanation: John 13:30: the physical night mirrors the darkness of the deed Judas had gone to do.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul taught that whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of profaning the body and blood of the Lord. He therefore urged believers to
questions.A: examine themselves before partaking
questions.B: abstain from the supper for the rest of their lives
questions.C: eat a full meal at home first
questions.D: receive the supper only from an apostle
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 11:27-29: 'Let a man examine himself, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Before the Sanhedrin many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony did not agree. Jesus was finally condemned when
questions.A: he answered 'I am' to the high priest's question whether he was the Christ, the Son of the Blessed
questions.B: two witnesses agreed that he had planned to burn down the temple during the coming Passover feast
questions.C: Judas testified before the council that Jesus had claimed to be king of the Jews in place of Caesar
questions.D: Peter admitted under oath in the courtyard that Jesus had blasphemed against the name of God
questions.explanation: Mark 14:55-64: the high priest tore his garments and said, 'You have heard his blasphemy.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Pilate asked Jesus, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' Jesus replied that his kingship was not of this world, otherwise
questions.A: his servants would have fought to prevent his being handed over to the Jews
questions.B: he would have accepted the crown the crowd offered him in Galilee
questions.C: Herod would have been removed from his throne
questions.D: the Roman legions would have joined his army
questions.explanation: John 18:36: Jesus' kingdom is spiritual and does not advance by violence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Pilate's wife sent word to him, 'Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much over him today in a dream.' Pilate nevertheless condemned Jesus because
questions.A: he feared a riot and wished to satisfy the crowd
questions.B: Jesus had confessed to leading an armed rebellion
questions.C: Herod had ordered him to carry out the sentence
questions.D: the witnesses had proved that Jesus blasphemed Caesar
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:19, 24-26: Pilate washed his hands, declared himself innocent of Jesus' blood, and released Barabbas.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: A magistrate who knows an accused person is innocent but convicts him to avoid the anger of a mob is acting like
questions.A: Pilate, who delivered Jesus to be crucified to satisfy the crowd
questions.B: Joseph of Arimathea, who asked for the body of Jesus
questions.C: Simon of Cyrene, who was compelled to carry the cross
questions.D: the centurion, who declared that Jesus was the Son of God
questions.explanation: Mark 15:15: 'Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released for them Barabbas... and delivered him to be crucified.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Herod Antipas questioned Jesus at length, hoping to see a sign, but Jesus
questions.A: made no answer at all
questions.B: performed a miracle to gain his release
questions.C: rebuked Herod for the murder of John the Baptist
questions.D: asked Herod to send him back to Galilee
questions.explanation: Luke 23:8-11: Herod and his soldiers treated him with contempt and sent him back to Pilate in a gorgeous robe.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: On the cross Jesus prayed, 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.' This prayer shows that
questions.A: he practised the love for enemies that he had taught
questions.B: he expected the soldiers to release him at once
questions.C: the soldiers had asked him for forgiveness
questions.D: he had forgotten the suffering he was enduring
questions.explanation: Luke 23:34: Jesus interceded for his executioners, fulfilling his own teaching in Matthew 5:44.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: The penitent thief said, 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom,' and Jesus replied,
questions.A: 'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise.'
questions.B: 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!'
questions.C: 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?'
questions.D: 'It is finished.'
questions.explanation: Luke 23:42-43: salvation was granted to a dying criminal who turned to Jesus in faith.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Jesus' cry, 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' expresses
questions.A: the depth of his suffering as he bore the sin of the world, in the words of Psalm 22
questions.B: his regret that he had ever come to Jerusalem instead of remaining safely in Galilee
questions.C: his doubt about whether God existed, since no rescue had come from heaven
questions.D: a call to Elijah to come down from heaven and rescue him from the cross
questions.explanation: Mark 15:34 quotes Psalm 22:1; bystanders wrongly thought he was calling Elijah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: The Roman centurion who stood facing Jesus said, 'Truly this man was the Son of God!' after he saw
questions.A: the manner in which Jesus breathed his last
questions.B: the soldiers dividing his garments by casting lots
questions.C: Joseph of Arimathea taking the body down
questions.D: the guards fleeing from the tomb
questions.explanation: Mark 15:39: a Gentile soldier confessed what the religious leaders denied.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council who was looking for the kingdom of God, 'took courage and went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus'. His act was courageous because
questions.A: it openly identified him with a man the council had condemned
questions.B: Pilate had ordered that anyone who touched the body be killed
questions.C: he had to fight the soldiers for the body
questions.D: the tomb he provided belonged to the high priest
questions.explanation: Mark 15:42-46: a secret disciple came into the open at the moment of greatest danger.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The women who came to the tomb early on the first day of the week were wondering who would roll away the stone. They found that
questions.A: the stone was rolled back and a young man in a white robe told them Jesus had risen
questions.B: the soldiers were still guarding the sealed tomb and refused to let them come near it
questions.C: Peter and John had already removed the body and carried it away to Galilee
questions.D: the stone had been broken into pieces by an earthquake and the tomb was full of rubble
questions.explanation: Mark 16:1-6: 'He has risen, he is not here; see the place where they laid him.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The angel told the women, 'Go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you to Galilee.' The special mention of Peter shows that
questions.A: Peter, despite his denial, was not cast off but included in the restoration
questions.B: Peter was already the head of the church in Jerusalem
questions.C: Peter had been absent from the other disciples since the arrest
questions.D: the angel did not regard Peter as a disciple any more
questions.explanation: Mark 16:7: grace reached out to the disciple who had failed most publicly.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Mary Magdalene mistook the risen Jesus for the gardener until
questions.A: he called her by her name
questions.B: he showed her his hands and his side
questions.C: he broke bread in her presence
questions.D: Peter arrived and identified him
questions.explanation: John 20:14-16: 'Jesus said to her, Mary. She turned and said to him in Hebrew, Rabboni!'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: On the road to Emmaus, Jesus said to the two disciples, 'O foolish men, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory?' He then
questions.A: interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself
questions.B: vanished immediately without saying anything more
questions.C: sent them back to Jerusalem to tell Peter
questions.D: showed them the wounds in his hands and feet
questions.explanation: Luke 24:25-27: the risen Christ opened the scriptures, beginning with Moses and all the prophets.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The chief priests gave the soldiers money to say, 'His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep.' The weakness of this story is that
questions.A: sleeping soldiers could not have known who took the body
questions.B: the disciples were in Galilee at the time
questions.C: the tomb had no stone to be moved
questions.D: the soldiers were Jewish and not Roman
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:11-15: the bribe and the contradictory story show the leaders' desperation to deny the resurrection.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus appeared to the disciples and they thought they saw a spirit, he said, 'Handle me, and see; for a spirit has not flesh and bones as you see that I have,' and he
questions.A: ate a piece of broiled fish before them
questions.B: walked on the water of the lake
questions.C: disappeared through the locked door
questions.D: washed their feet once more
questions.explanation: Luke 24:36-43: the risen Jesus demonstrated that his resurrection was bodily, not a ghostly apparition.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: By the Sea of Tiberias Jesus asked Peter three times, 'Simon, son of John, do you love me?' and each time charged him, 'Feed my sheep.' The threefold question corresponded to
questions.A: Peter's three denials, allowing him to be publicly restored
questions.B: the three years Peter had followed Jesus
questions.C: the three booths Peter had wanted to build
questions.D: the three thousand who would be converted at Pentecost
questions.explanation: John 21:15-17: Peter was grieved at the third question, but the threefold commission reinstated him as shepherd.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Before his ascension Jesus told the apostles, 'You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth.' This verse gives
questions.A: the programme of the church's mission, beginning at home and spreading to the whole world
questions.B: a promise that the apostles would rule Israel from Jerusalem
questions.C: an instruction to remain in Jerusalem permanently
questions.D: the date on which the Holy Spirit would come
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8: the outline of the book of Acts follows this geographical expansion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: As the apostles gazed into heaven after the ascension, two men in white robes told them that
questions.A: this Jesus would come again in the same way as they saw him go into heaven
questions.B: Jesus had gone to Galilee and would meet them there
questions.C: they should elect a new leader in place of Jesus
questions.D: the kingdom would be restored to Israel that very year
questions.explanation: Acts 1:10-11: the ascension carries the promise of the second coming.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church member says, 'The resurrection is only a symbol that Jesus' ideas live on.' The gospel accounts contradict this because
questions.A: the risen Jesus was touched, ate food and showed his wounds
questions.B: the disciples never actually saw Jesus after his death
questions.C: the tomb was never found empty
questions.D: Jesus appeared only in dreams to the disciples
questions.explanation: Luke 24:39-43 and John 20:27: the evangelists stress the physical reality of the resurrection body.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After feeding the five thousand Jesus said, 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger.' He meant that
questions.A: he alone satisfies the deepest spiritual need of humanity
questions.B: he would provide free bread daily for his followers
questions.C: his followers would never need to eat ordinary food
questions.D: the manna in the wilderness had been his own body
questions.explanation: John 6:35: the crowd sought loaves; Jesus pointed them to himself as the food that endures to eternal life.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I am the light of the world; he who follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.' A person who claims to follow Jesus but lives in deliberate sin
questions.A: contradicts this claim, since following the light means leaving darkness
questions.B: is walking in the light because he goes to church
questions.C: shows that light and darkness can coexist in a disciple
questions.D: proves that the light of life is a future reward only
questions.explanation: John 8:12; 1 John 1:6: 'If we say we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I am the door; if any one enters by me, he will be saved.' This claim means that
questions.A: he is the only way of entry into salvation and the fold of God
questions.B: the temple gate had been closed to Gentiles
questions.C: his followers should build churches with narrow doors
questions.D: salvation is available through any religious teacher
questions.explanation: John 10:7-9: the shepherd's door image stresses exclusive access through Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live.' He spoke these words to
questions.A: Martha, before raising her brother Lazarus
questions.B: Mary Magdalene, at the empty tomb
questions.C: Thomas, after the resurrection
questions.D: Nicodemus, when he came by night
questions.explanation: John 11:25-27: Martha responded, 'Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser... Apart from me you can do nothing.' Jesus was teaching that
questions.A: fruitful Christian life depends on continual union with him
questions.B: farming is the most suitable occupation for Christians
questions.C: the Father prunes only the branches that bear no fruit
questions.D: believers can bear fruit through their own strength
questions.explanation: John 15:1-5: 'He who abides in me, and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A church worker who used to be effective becomes proud, stops praying and gradually loses all influence for good. His experience illustrates Jesus' saying,
questions.A: 'Apart from me you can do nothing.'
questions.B: 'The Son of man came not to be served but to serve.'
questions.C: 'Before Abraham was, I am.'
questions.D: 'I am the good shepherd.'
questions.explanation: John 15:5: a branch cut off from the vine withers; effectiveness flows from abiding in Christ.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When Jesus said, 'Before Abraham was, I am,' the Jews took up stones to throw at him because
questions.A: he was claiming the divine name and eternal existence
questions.B: he had insulted Abraham, their father
questions.C: he claimed to be older than Moses
questions.D: it was unlawful to mention Abraham in the temple
questions.explanation: John 8:58-59: 'I am' echoes God's name in Exodus 3:14; the hearers understood it as a claim to deity.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'The Son of man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.' The word 'ransom' indicates that his death
questions.A: was the price paid to set sinners free
questions.B: was an unfortunate accident of history
questions.C: would be reversed by the payment of money
questions.D: freed only the twelve apostles
questions.explanation: Mark 10:45: Jesus interpreted his coming death as a redemptive, substitutionary act.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I and the Father are one,' and, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father.' These sayings teach
questions.A: the unity of the Son with the Father, so that Jesus reveals God fully
questions.B: that Jesus and the Father are the same person in different roles
questions.C: that the Father ceased to exist when the Son was born
questions.D: that Jesus was only a human prophet sent by God
questions.explanation: John 10:30 and 14:9: Jesus claimed a unique oneness with the Father while remaining distinct from him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A dying Christian tells her family, 'Do not weep for me; I am only going to the room he has prepared.' She is drawing on Jesus' promise,
questions.A: 'In my Father's house are many rooms... I go to prepare a place for you.'
questions.B: 'I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger.'
questions.C: 'I am the door of the sheep.'
questions.D: 'You are the light of the world.'
questions.explanation: John 14:2-3: 'I will come again and will take you to myself, that where I am you may be also.'
